newsitem.title: GERMANY: Heidelzement sees better 1996 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Heidelzement sees better 1996 net profit.

text.p: German building materials company Heidelberger Zement AG said on Friday that it expected to report an improved net profit for 1996, with sales at least matching the year-ago level.

In its mid-year report, Heidelzement said that its sales fell by around one percent in the first half of the year to 2.88 billion marks ($1.9 billion). It gave no profit figures. ($ = 1.483 German Marks)

For 1995, Heidelzement reported group net profit of 469 million marks ($316.1 million) compared with 362.3 million marks a year earlier. Its sales were at 6.04 billion marks, down from 6.026 billion in 1994.
"Our expectations for the full year 1996 -- without taking into account newly-consolidated companies -- are along the lines of sales and net profit of the previous year," it said.
"Group net profit excluding third-party contributions will increase from 1995," it added in its statement.

Heidelzement, in common with other building industry groups, said that the extremely harsh winter had had a negative impact on its first half performance. But this had been offset to some extent by a growth trend in the United States, it said.

Heidelzement said that a shift of its business activities in general into foreign growth markets had helped to shield it from problems in the home market. Measures taken within Germany to optimise its performance there had also helped, it said.
